provider: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System)
dataset: VIIRS 375 m active fire detections, NOAA-20, near real-time (Area API)
description: Thermal anomalies / active fire pixels detected by the VIIRS instrument on NOAA-20 during the last two days, worldwide.

coverage.temporal: Most recent two days of near-real-time detections

updateCadence.upstream: Within about three hours of each satellite overpass

envVars.name: FIRMS_MAP_KEY
envVars.description: Free FIRMS MAP_KEY (32 characters) used in the Area API path.

auth.setup: Request a free MAP_KEY with your e-mail address at the FIRMS site, then set FIRMS_MAP_KEY in .env. The key allows 5,000 transactions per 10 minutes.

attribution: NASA FIRMS / LANCE – VIIRS 375 m active fire product (NOAA-20)

license.name: NASA Earth Science data – free and open; FIRMS asks for acknowledgement
license.notes: NASA EOSDIS data are free and open. Acknowledge: "We acknowledge the use of data and/or imagery from NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), part of NASA's Earth Science Data and Information System (ESDIS)."

limitations: A detection is a thermal anomaly in a ~375 m pixel, not a confirmed wildfire: gas flares, volcanoes, industrial heat and sun glint also trigger detections.
Cloud and thick smoke hide fires; each satellite sees a place only a few times per day, so short-lived fires are missed.
Near-real-time data are preliminary and are later replaced by standard-quality processing.
At most 100,000 detections per fetch are kept (highest fire radiative power first) to bound storage; low-confidence detections are kept and labelled.
The Suomi NPP VIIRS product suggested by older documentation no longer delivers new data; this adapter uses NOAA-20.
confidenceNotes: FIRMS classifies each VIIRS detection as low, nominal or high confidence. This application maps those classes to 0.3 / 0.6 / 0.9 (a derived, ordinal convenience – not a probability).

retention.note: Detections are purged three days after acquisition.

layers.name: Active fire detections (VIIRS)
layers.description: Satellite thermal anomalies from the last two days: density heat map at low zoom, individual detections when zoomed in.
